name: FlappyBird
author: NinjaLetter2160
description: Flappy Bird (PICO-8) A tiny retro remake of the classic one-button flyer, built entirely from 8x8 tiles. This is my first game, so go easy on me! Tap the X or O button to make the bird flap — let go and gravity takes over fast, so timing is everything. Weave through the gaps in the pipes without clipping the top, bottom, or floor to rack up your score. Miss one, and it's game over — press the button again to jump right back in. How to play: X or O button — flap / start / retry Each pipe you clear adds 1 to your score Touching a pipe, the ceiling, or the floor ends the run

name: pilatro_35
author: Jabz
description: Updates! This is my newest update to the Pico8 Balatro port. In this update I've added: Planet cards (hand levels) +17 new Joker cards Seudo Tarot cards (I'm not in love with how I've implemented tarot cards for the 8ball, will fix later) Controls: Mouse: select/drag | Holding Right click shows descriptions X: play/buy C: discard/sell Rules: Basically the same as base Balatro with some exclusion due to pico8 limitation + me probably being dumb. Core Game Structure Antes and Blinds: Each Ante consists of three rounds called Blinds: a Small Blind , a Big Blind , and a Boss Blind . Winning a Run: Successfully clear all 8 Antes to win the standard run. Turn and Hand Rules Drawing & Playing: You start round drawing 8 cards. You can play up to 5 cards from your hand to make a valid poker hand. Discards: You can discard up to 5 unwanted cards a limited number of times per round to try and draw better combinations. You cannot both play and discard on the same turn. Scoring Mechanics Scores are calculated using a two-part math system: Chips x Mult (Chips are base points from the cards, multiplied by your multiplier). Cards: Base values of played cards add to your Chips. Left-to-Right Order: Scoring resolves from left to right, meaning card placement and the positioning of your Jokers matter significantly for maximizing addition and multiplication. The Shop & Enhancements After beating a blind, you enter the Shop to spend money earned from remaining hands. interest, and base income. Jokers: Up to 5 special modifier cards that drastically break rules and boost chips or multipliers. Planet Cards: Upgrade the base level, chips, and mult of specific poker hands. Tarot & Spectral Cards: Modify, destroy, duplicate, or change the suits and enhancements of individual playing cards in your deck. NOTE: current version of cart only sort of implements Tarot Cards with 8ball joker and has no implementation of Spectral Cards . Though you can add cards to your deck with bonuses through the Pack in the shop. Currently these are all of the 35 available Joker cards: NOTE: There are likely to be many bugs with jokers please let me know what you find?

name: Princess Mochi
author: astropelican
description: Princess Mochi has a jetpack, two pigtails that never quite keep up with her, and a whole town's worth of mochi to carry home before dark. UFOs always flank her in single file, then dive straight into her. [8x8] The pigeons mean well. They fan in, arrange themselves into a very tidy little ring, and shoot at her anyway. [8x8] Fishcakes aren't meanies exactly, they're just happily wiggling through their little ribbon dance, unfortunately right in her way. [8x8] The mech means it rather more. And somewhere past the second town something enormous is waiting, though she'd rather not think about that part just yet. [16x16] Mochi is the whole point. [16x16] Pink mochi makes her gun quicker and her reach longer. These appear whenever she terminates an enemy fool that gets in her way. [16x16] Cream mochi makes her light on her feet. These appear when she obliterates an entire wave of pigeons, UFOs, or fishcakes. [16x16] Matcha mochi, her favorite, buys hearts, and hearts are the one thing nobody can take back off her; clip a tree or a road sign and everything else goes bouncing merrily away down the road behind you. Embarrassing, but survivable. Two towns, two bosses, and one princess with excellent posture and no intention of slowing down. 🤍 Special thanks to the pico8 Discord community for their help: freds72 who was instrumental in helping me nail the shadow aesthetic, and @wasdly for the mode7 terrain rendering, as well as the #project channel on there for feedback and suggestions. Parens-8 Built with parens-8, which is AGPLv3. Full source here. download Windows, Mac, Linux, and Raspberry PI builds from itch.io.

name: Kairu
author: sgchild9
description: Kairu A strategic territory game inspired by Kulami, made for PICO-8. Place your marbles to claim territory while restricting where your opponent can play next. The board gradually changes as spaces are occupied, creating a game where a move that looks good now can set up — or ruin — your next several turns. Kairu includes: Single-player mode with an easy/hard AI opponent Local 2-player mode Territory-based scoring Condensed rules included in cartridge but full ruleset can be found online This started as an experiment to see if I could build a Kulami-inspired game in PICO-8, and gradually turned into a proper little game of its own. Enjoy!

name: Plight of the Angel
author: AlrtCypress
description: Survive the boss for as long as you can! Controls: Use LEFT, RIGHT, and UP (or X if you're using a controller) to fly around. Press O to dash. Press DOWN to heal (as long as the cooldown is not active.) Tips: the screen wraps around. Use it to dodge attacks if needed. your hitbox is relatively small. It's never too late to squeeze out to safety! there is no cooldown on the dash ability. Just be careful not to dash right into an attack! This game was inspired by late-game Terraria bosses, including the wing-based movement and the bullet hell gameplay. Let me know what you think! Attack Patterns: Red: A cluster of projectiles spawn offscreen, locking onto you then firing. Yellow: 3 small dots spawn around you and quickly accelerate inward. Purple: 6 dots begin to swirl around you, slowly closing in. Green: Bouncing balls fall from the sky from left to right (or vice versa) and bounce back up ======Changelog ====== 1.01 day-one hotfix for controller support. Press X to fly upward. 1.02 fixed a bug where X and UP had different flying physics. Adjusted the music and introduced Autoheal 1.03 added cover art, updated description to add attack descriptions 1.04 added a new alternate song. The music is picked randomly at game start

description: This is my first foray into development using Pico-8, I enjoyed it a lot! I tried to give the game a couple Easter eggs and oddities, to give it a slightly different flavour from other minesweeper clones. Controls: Arrow Keys - movement C - Reveal a square // Confirm X - Toggle flag The mouse controls are as you'd expect. (Player 2's controls are Pico-8's defaults) For the Name menu, you can change letters using the Up and Down keys, and move between character positions using Right and Left. Features: Click on Yeller (the smiley face) in the upper right of the board, he'll give you a hint that might be useful. Full mouse support (besides the versus mode and name selection screen), persistent hi-scores and user-selected names. (I'll leave the Easter eggs a mystery) If you find any notable bugs, please let me know! I very likely missed many .

name: Palace 2.0
author: rozaporx
description: Setup & Table Layout  Face-Down Palace: Deal 3 cards face-down in a row in front of each player. These remain secret until the end of the game.  Face-Up Palace: Deal 3 cards face-up, directly on top of each face-down card.  In-Hand Cards: Deal 6 cards face-down to each player to form their initial hand.  Draw Pile: Place the remaining deck face-down in the center of the table. Leave space next to it for the discard pile.  The Swap Phase: Before play begins, each player may swap cards between their 6 hand cards and their 3 face-up Palace cards. Use this phase to put your strongest cards (e.g., 2s, 10s, Aces) into your face-up Palace. LAYOUT TIP: Your Palace consists of 3 hidden face-down cards with 3 visible face-up cards resting on top of them. You cannot play these until the central draw pile is exhausted and your hand is completely empty. Special & Power Cards Power cards break standard rank progression and give tactical advantages: Card Role Special Effect & Rules 2 Reset Card Resets the play pile value to zero. Can be played on TOP of any card, and ANY card can be played on top of a 2. 10 Burn Card Immediately clears (burns) the entire discard pile from the game. The player takes an immediate extra turn. 4-of-a-Kind Automatic Burn Playing four cards of the same rank consecutively (or stacking 4 at once) instantly burns the pile and grants an extra turn. Gameplay Loop • Playing Cards: On your turn, play a card that is equal to or higher in rank than the top card on the discard pile. You may play multiple cards of the same rank together (e.g., two 8s or three 5s). • Drawing Cards: As long as cards remain in the central draw pile, you must always maintain at least 3 cards in your hand. Draw back up to 3 immediately after completing your play. • Picking Up the Pile: If you cannot play a valid card (or choose not to), you must pick up the ENTIRE discard pile and add it to your hand. Your turn then ends. Transitioning to the Palace & Winning Once the central draw pile is completely exhausted and your hand is empty, you access your Palace: Step 1 — Play Face-Up Cards: Play from your 3 face-up cards using standard rules. You can play matching multiples if you have them. Step 2 — Play Blind Face-Down Cards: Once all face-up cards are gone, flip your face-down cards one at a time on your turn without looking beforehand. Success vs. Penalty: If the flipped card is a valid play, it stays in the pile and your turn ends. If it is invalid, you MUST pick up the entire discard pile along with that card. You must then clear your hand again before returning to your remaining hidden Palace cards. VICTORY: The first player to successfully clear all hand cards, face-up cards, and blind face-down cards wins the game!

name: D&D Fifth Edition Armor Piece Calculator
author: sirdoodle16
description: This is a simple calculator for a rule to have armor sets split into 3 different slots for D&D Fifth Edition. Extra rules are as follows, as well as the formula used below. STR requirements to wear armors still apply, with the required number being decreased by 1 for each missing piece of armor from the full set. Extra features such as stealth disadvantage or adding DEX bonus only apply if 2 out of your 3 armor slots have armors that use that feature. If you are wearing one piece of armor with an uncapped DEX bonus, and one with DEX bonus capped at +2, your DEX bonus will be capped at +2. Armor that is enchanted to be +1/+2/+3 can vary in where it is enchanted. If an entire set is enchanted, then the bonus from the enchantment is applied only to the Set Bonus category, and does not happen without wearing the full armor set. If a specific piece of armor is enchanted however, the bonus only applies when wearing that specific piece of armor. When wearing multiple pieces of enchanted armor from different sets, only the higher bonus applies, with the other being nullified. If two pieces of enchanted armor are from the same set, the bonuses stack. The formula explained: In order to calculate how much AC each individual piece grants, you must first determine an armor's AC “score”. The score can be found by taking the base AC of the armor, and subtracting 10 from it. The score does not include extra bonuses such as DEX modifier for leather armor, or the +1/+2/+3 from enchanted armor. Once you have the armor’s score, you must then divide that up into 4 different categories, each representing one of the armor pieces, with the fourth representing the bonus for wearing the entire set. The order of the categories always follows Set Bonus -> Torso -> Legs -> Head. To distribute these points, you place 1 point in the first category, then move onto the next, looping back to the first category when you hit the last one. Once an armor set runs out of points, no more points should be placed into any categories. Each point in a category counts as +1 AC for wearing that piece of armor, while the set bonus is only applied when wearing the full set of armor. The final AC calculation adds the bonuses to your base AC of 10. DEX modifiers that are applicable to certain armors are still applied once to the final AC. Examples of this formula can be found at the end of this section.

description: The Game Turn-based science fiction game. Build space ships to explore Mercury, Mars, and other worlds to gather data about their resources. Your research facility develops new spacecraft to colonize these worlds. Dispatch vessels to asteroids to collect small amounts of resources, and expand by building stations on explored worlds until you reach the farthest edges of our solar system. Controls Use the arrow keys to move the green cursor and press X to select options. For the date icon: Press to advance one turn, or hold to speed up - though the game will pause automatically if an event occurs. Use the first icon to return to The Moon base. The second icon lets you switch to bases on other worlds - if you’ve built any. I’m not sure how much of the game to explain - some players might prefer to discover things on their own. But if you’d like more hints, I will add them here. Development Inspired by old Amiga classics like Millennium 2.2 and Deuteros, I programmed until PICO-8 memory ran out. The game now includes planets and moons, stations and spaceships, and even a short intro and an ending sequence. Due to memory contraints, missions are limited and straightforward - no enemies or combat here. Balancing was tricky, and creating music, sound effects, and pixel art was new to me. Even so, experimenting with PICO-8 is a lot of fun, and I’m still working on improvements. Version History 0.9.2 - solved bug: wrong resource index when mars was colonized before mercury; removed the "game" menu topic 0.9.1 - in the 'Production' menu, an ongoing production can no longer be canceled by selecting another product (which previously resulted in resource loss) 0.9 - first upload

name: mandelbrot_v2
author: Jenques
description: The Mandelbrot set This is a plot of the number of recursions it takes for a point (on a complex plane) to either form a cycle or fly off to infinity. Pico-8 has a limit on the precision of numbers so you can only zoom in so much. Technically speaking though there is an infinite amount to explore. Controls: Use your arrows to pan around and circle and cross to zoom. Colour Palette: To change the colour palette, open the pause menu with P or ENTER, and cycle through the options with your arrow keys. Press enter, P, circle or cross to close. Recursion Limit and Exponent: These values can be tweaked in menu like the colour palette to your liking. A higher recursion limit allows you to see finer detail in the fractal at the expense of performance. The exponent is purely for aesthetics, and allows you to change how the colours are rendered. (This may need some tweaking and changes) Version 2.4 change log and a note on higher precision: Hidden colours added to improve colour gradients. Added colour invert setting. Improved gradient calculation. (Further improvements needed, suggestions welcome) On higher precision: I vibe coded an experiment with combining variables to improve precision, however the functions impact performance a lot, so there's little point in publishing it. Though I would have to implement it by hand in order to publish, at this stage I don't think it's worth it. Let me know your thoughts on if it can be done efficiently or if you'd like to see it anyway. Version 2.3 change log and future plans: Optimised performance by refactoring code, removing expensive maths calls, localising variables and streamlining the frame drawing process. NOTE: Claude did suggest some of these but all code was written by hand. Menu buttons for recursion limit and exponent added. New green colour palette added. Coming soon : More colour palettes! secondary colour palette? (done) Replace exponent with better colour space maths... (done-ish) Investigation into compound numbers for very fine detail rendering. (done -- not worth it) Recursion functions with exponents other than two i.e. Zn = Zn^3+C This has been a great project and it's been amazing to see people appreciate it as much as I have. I'm happy with what I've achieved in this. Besides the expanded colour palette, the other future features may be a while off due to the research they will require and may be part of a new version 3 if I can call it that. Version 1 is not on BBS but there are many others like it, I thought it was too ugly to post xD. name: Beeventure!
author: Zandor
description: This is my first PICO-8 game! I had a lot of fun making it and I hope you like playing it. Let me know what you think! BEEVENTURE You're a bee with one year to live. Gather pollen, turn it into honey, and store up enough to survive the winter. THE GOAL Collect 20 honey before winter ends. Each season runs 2.5 minutes, so a full year is about ten minutes. The world changes with the seasons -- the palette shifts, the flowers change, and it snows in winter. CONTROLS ⬅️ ➡️ move ❎ hold to fly, let go to drop 🅾️ call your helper bees back to you (also revives you when you die) HOW IT WORKS Land on a flower to collect pollen -- you can carry 4 to start. Fly home and land on the hive to deposit it. The honeycomb holds 16 pollen. Every time you fill it you get: +4 honey +1 helper bee (up to 4) +1 health, if you're hurt So 20 honey means filling the comb five times. Flowers regrow after a while, so you never run the world dry. HELPER BEES Your helper bees follow you and pick fights with the flies. Each one also raises how much pollen you can carry, up to 8 with a full crew. They're fragile -- three hits and they're gone -- and when one dies your carrying capacity drops with it. Press 🅾️ to pull them out of a fight before they get killed, and bring them back to the hive to heal them up. WATCH OUT Flies cost you a heart on contact, and you only have four. Run out and you'll wake up back at the start with full health -- but you'll drop every scrap of pollen you were carrying. Press 🅾️ on the title screen for in-game help.

description: You're a frog in a generated maze. Eat every pip to clear it. Two kinds of pip [8x8] Normal pips are everywhere. You'll have plenty. [8x8] Rubies only appear when a frenzied ghost is within three tiles of you. While one is that close, every pip you eat turns red. Get far enough away and they turn normal again. Play it safe and you'll finish the maze with a pile of normal pips and nothing worth spending them on. To get rich, you have to let the ghosts get close. Ghosts [8x8] [8x8] [8x8] [8x8] Ghosts wander the maze looking for frenzy pills. They avoid you, until they eat one. A wandering ghost is food. Run into it and you eat it for pips. But when a ghost eats a frenzy pill it turns red and hunts you for about ten seconds. If it catches you, you lose 90% of your pips, both colours. It also eats your auto-frogs. Frenzy pills [8x8] Frenzy pills are what set the ghosts off. One flashes for a second before appearing, with a strange little sound. You can eat one yourself for 10 normal pips and 5 rubies. Doing so also calms every frenzied ghost in the maze. Fruit [8x8] [8x8] [8x8] Fruit puffs in away from you and hops around. Catch it and it bursts into pips that fly out and then home in on you. Strawberry 5, blueberry 10, eggplant 15. The longer you go without being caught, the better the fruit. Leave it too long and it puffs away. Ghosting [8x8] Press ❎ to turn into a ghost. Nothing can catch you. It only lasts half a second to start with. Upgrade it in the shop, half a second at a time, up to two seconds. You cannot eat while vanished — no pips, no pills, no fruit. The blue meter drains while you are a ghost and refills when you are not. Clearing a maze Clear one without being caught: PERFECT . Eat five or more of one ghost type: MASSACRE . Both: PERFECT MASSACRE . Mazes get harder. Your best clear time and longest perfect streak are saved. Parens-8 Built with parens-8, which is AGPLv3. name: Do Not Win This Tic Tac Toe
author: BiosStudio
description: DO NOT WIN THIS TIC TAC TOE because the win condition is twisted. The normal Tic Tac Toe rules apply but you have to master all 8 abilities. Every round you can gain 5 points for every line , or use your random abilities to get more points. Maybe this is not a solved game anymore. Maybe if you unlock more abilities, you will know what the true ending is. Maybe the only winning move is... DO NOT WIN THIS TIC TAC TOE Gameplay Play against CPU as the main game mode. Offline 2 player mode available once unlocked. Press (X), X to continue/place tile Press (O), Z to display information on abilities Press arrow keys to move the cursor +5 pts for every horizontal, vertical, and diagonal line You can restart the game by pressing Enter/Game Menu button Abilities KING +4pts if you place a tile on the center CROSSBOW +1pts for every tiles placed on each corner SIDEMAN +1pts for every tiles placed on each side Spoilers for other abilities below PEACEMAKER +5pts even if the game ends in a draw MAGICIAN Every turn: Enemy only has 3 tiles, your pts -1 for every vanished tiles STOMPER Every round: You can replace enemy tile once (except for the most recent one) RABBIT Always goes first, randomise if the enemy is also a rabbit GAMBLER Every turn: There is a 10% chance to place 2 tiles Credits Special thanks to NerdyTeachers and LazyDevs for their tutorials which got me into game development in PICO-8. Thanks to voidgazerbon for playtest, and all the people in the Discord community for their continuous support. Thanks to the many amazing tools and carts in this forum which were there when I am confused with programming. It's my first time coding so I try my best to credit the relevant tools/functions in the cart itself. Lastly, thanks for reading up to this point and playing the game. Changelog 23 August 2026: Unlock conditions now correctly check from the latest game instead of total game won and lost. (Don't worry if you accidentally unlock abilities, you deserve it anyway!) 25 August 2026: Change the description to Offline 2 Player Mode for clarity. Currently published on itch.io !

name: Orbitwell
author: rufenerd
description: Fly by science and by feel in this space gravity physics adventure! Complete missions as you advance your spaceflight skills. Flight Controls x: thrust; increase translational velocity in the rocket's current angle left: increase angular velocity; rotate counter-clockwise faster or clockwise slower right: decrease angular velocity; rotate clockwise faster or counter-clockwise slower z: display alternate stats (for select missions) pause: menu option to restart mission Flight Telemetry Gauges x: distance to the right of the center of Earth, negative is to the left y: distance above the center of Earth, negative is down θ: your rocket's current angle; radians/pi dx: horizontal velocity; distance to the right per frame dy: vertical velocity; distance up per frame dθ: angular velocity in the counter-clockwise direction r: distance from center of earth |v|: speed; magnitude of velocity relative to Earth blue: speed is too slow to achieve circular orbit red: speed is too high to achieve circular orbit green: speed is close or exactly right for circular orbit orbv: required velocity for circular orbit at given r; sqrt(GM/r) blue: orbit target velocity is below current rocket velocity red: orbit target velocity is above current rocket velocity green: orbit target velocity is near current rocket velocity ecc: orbital eccentricity to Earth; how oval-shaped the orbit is red: orbit is too oval-shaped to orbit orange: orbit might be possible, but not sustainable green: circular orbit achieved relv: relative speed between the rocket and another mass dist: distance from the rocket and another mass relative crash v: relative speed between the rocket and what it crashed into Background Inspired by my physics class, the gravity and mechanics are as physically realistic as I could make them. Much is not to scale (space is huge, gravity is weak), though some things are. Hint Strategic flying and patience can be just as good as ace flying control, but either can work! Code Reuse and AI Disclosure This entirety of this game's code, sprites, sfx, and music were designed and built by me, except: Sprite rotation code and ideas from https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?pid=52525 (thank you all, especially @jihem and @Gabe_8_bit ) I occasionally used LLMs as a physics and astronomy reference, including for how to calculate eccentricity given the mechanics data I had readily available in my game; see code comment for details

name: NHS Manager
author: Mighty_Pirate
description: I've been playing around with PICO-8 to explore what it might be like to use for computer game art and philosophy. Here's my latest: NHS Manager A tiny art-game about public healthcare in modern Britain. "This was the first time I addressed a contemporary political issue in an art-game. I thought it would be interesting to make a simple simulator about being a manager of an NHS hospital. I used to play games like Theme Hospital and Sim City. They always had a sharp satirical edge, something that was lost as the genre developed in the 2000s. Given the pressures on the NHS today, I wanted to go back to that. Like many people in Britain, I've received fantastic care from the NHS. But there's also times when I've been let down. And I've lived through all the rounds of 'reforms'. I even worked as a healthcare assistant for a bit, back at the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital when I was first swapping PICO-8 carts. This game is both a love letter to and a playful satire of an institution that we need more than ever." -- James LaGrande If you enjoyed this game, please consider donating to the NHS or, better yet, writing to your MP in support. Controls Arrow keys to select (X) and (Z) to confirm
